output.summary: Yellow-flowering wood-sorrel native to South Africa. Its abundant underground bulbs help make it a difficult-to-eradicate invasive weed elsewhere. In South Africa it is a traditional stew ingredient; modest amounts are described as reasonably harmless, while boiling food parts can reduce oxalate-related risks.
output.edibilityNote: Traditional South African stew ingredient; leaves, roots or fleshy underground runners are eaten, with boiling advised to reduce risks from high calcium oxalate.
